decisions.reason: F1 uses canonical map, not canonical transformation: def-cm-finite-regularity-canonical-calculus explicitly defines a C1 canonical map by pointwise pullback preservation without injectivity. The cited prop-cm-canonical-map-tests-and-hamiltonian-transport clause 1 proves exactly its matrix test. All displayed examples are linear maps on the full Euclidean phase domains; the canonicity tests, grouped-coordinate shear and alternating four-linear determinant computation are valid. No global invertibility claim for arbitrary C1 maps occurs.

F3 omitted the residual generalized force: supplier clause 2 gives Pdot=-Htilde_q+Qres, so identification with X_Htilde requires Qres=0 along the curve (in particular d=0). This is a nonfatal overstatement in the explanatory fact: all four stated transport conclusions concern arbitrary Hamiltonian systems and follow independently from the square symplectic derivative identity and the chain rule. Repaired F3 to retain this source qualification, and corrected F2 from the ill-typed (f composed with C) derivative to (C composed with z) derivative. Statement, physical_scope, dependency list and all proof steps are unchanged.

The numerical scope falsely called partial maps canonical transformations onto their declared target U. With U=(0,1)^2, M=1, V=0 and h=1/2, the admissible Verlet domain is {0<p<1, 0<q<1-p/2}; its image is {0<P<1, P/2<Q<1}, a proper subset of U. Hence the claimed global transformation is false, although the derivative preserves J. Repaired Numerics and physical_scope to local canonical transformations, allowing canonical transformations only onto the open image. The cited proposition establishes exactly this qualification; its inverse factors also justify the onto-image statement.
